generated_text: Rather annoying when the phone keeps beeping in the middle of trying to get the baby down, isn't it?      Yes, poor thing. I can't imagine how we managed with a little one before all this tech. Did you ever get those things to work properly?      Not really, I gave up one night and handed over to his dad instead. He sorted it out with that magical men stuff.      Haha, typical. It was easier pulling teeth to get him to tidy the living room for once!      You won’t get any argument from me. So, speaking of our kids, we need to plan something for Lewis’ 16th soon, don’t we?      Yes! I had the date earmarked on the diary and I think he’d like something with most of the lads and girls. Maybe breakfast, rides and then a proper party.      That’s the classic oversized birthday we used to have back in the day, minus the overindulgence—vastly preferable, don’t you think?      Definitely! Here to there and grief. Speaking of old ways, aren’t you meeting up with Claire and Jan tomorrow then?      Mate, I’ve been meaning to speak to you about that! I’ve had a last minute call about that freelance thing and Jan’s asked if I could swap with her.      Who with? That new lad from work or something?      Funny you mention it. It is him. Sam wants to talk it through and see if I’m up for doing more stuff for him about marketing his business. Seems okay but I'll need the extra time this week.      Going into that extra work and child-rearing is a tough one but if the money’s good for the odd lesson or guest speaker thing at the school, that’s always appreciated.      Do you know, I hadn't even thought of that. Might come in handy for Charlotte and that art thing of hers.      That’s what I do with the extra cash. Even set aside a bit for Lewis and some gadgets the kids can enjoy.      Smart. If I can manage it, I'll suggest that to Sam. It could go further than just the usual payout.      You're seriously clever with this sort of thing, you always were, never had to worry about making it worth it.      We were lucky! It's a relief I can pay for one of these evenings when the baby is being a supreme little nightmare.

Rather annoying, though—queuein’ up at the border for five hours just ’cos we’ve suddenly got to show our passports again. I’m talkin’ about my holiday in Spain last September. Thought I’d hear the sun, only to spend the first day stuck at a motorway service station.       laughs  Sounds like one o’ them days where Brexit's actually hit you in the face. A lot o’ folk I talk to just don’t get why it makes a difference, y’know. We’ve been to the same beaches every summer for years, but now it’s suddenly different... like we’ve lost some kind o’ identity.      That’s the weird thing about it. I still speak to my Cypriot cousin Anna, and she doesn’t see the difference at all. But I used to think o’ her place in Larnaca as a sort o’ weekend breakfast, no stress. Now I’m ditherin’ in my head over whether I should book a holiday flight, ’cos I don’t fancy the hassle.      I can see that. I applied for my Erasmus PhD grant, and it was like pullin’ teeth. They kept askin’ for proofs of residency, extra documents... Suddenly, being British meant I was ‘a third country national’ in their system. My Italian supervisor was like, “You weren’t this complicated before.”       laughs  Tell me about it. I remember the old days. I did an undergrad in France—just my student ID and I was good to go. Never had to think about it. Now I’m talkin’ to mates and they’re panicin’ over visas for Portugal, like it’s suddenly a different world.      It’s ironic, innit? We always joked that the EU was a bit of a farce, but when the rules actually  change —y’expected inconvenience, but it’s more than that. Like, the whole vibe shifts. Travel feels like an admin nightmare now instead o’ a holiday.       pours another pint  Y’gotta hand it to the French, though. I took the Eurotunnel for once, and they had tannoy announcin’, “British passengers may need to present additional documents.” If it was anyone else, I’d chuckle. But it’s our own lives bloomin’ getting harder.      I know, right? I still think we’ll adapt. Maybe in a year or two, it’ll be forgotten. But for now, it’s like Europe’s learnin’ to not trust us all over again.

Rather than share a dessert, we play Monopoly again, do we need to set it out?      No, no mummy, just talking about it. I've been saving my pocket money for sweets.      Be very careful with spending. We could make some Lemon Cake, if you liked.      I want some cherries as well.      I want some custard too.      Well, if you like it. We can have both cherries and custard. But, be warned, we won’t get everything we want in Monopoly.      What is Monopoly?      It's a game, you buy properties and collect money.      And what if you run out of money?      Then you’ve lost the game. You need to manage your money carefully, just like when you spend your pocket money on sweets.      I always have so much money. I don't know what to spend it on, apart from sweets and toys.      What about saving some for a bigger toy, like a book or action figures?      I like building blocks.      Building blocks are great. Let's talk about desserts today. Would you like some apple pie, or chocolate brownies?      I like chocolate, but I also like someone who makes apple pie.      I like cake best.      Well, let's compromise. Maybe a chocolate cake with apple pie for your grandmother, or would you prefer ice cream as well?      Only if it is vanilla. I don’t like strawberry.      Then vanilla it is. Now, back to Monopoly, shall we start the game?      Yes, I want to be the one who has the most money at the end.      I hope I win as well, and I’ll buy all the houses.      Well, we must manage our money carefully in Monopoly, and also around sweets and desserts! Anyone up for some go-fund on snacks later if you win?      Yeah! I could buy some sweets with the monopoly money.      But what if you only get it to buy and then someone else lands on those properties?      Exactly, it’s about investing over time, not just spending all at once. Now, who buys what first?      I'll buy the first one always, so I can make money quickly.      I will buy the largest ones as soon as I have enough.      Great, then let's begin. May the best house-buyer win! And when we're done, we can go into the kitchen and make something sweet. Deal?      Deal!      Deal! Let's settle the game fast.

Rather annoying this, innit? Traffic’s mental again, stuck outside the roundabout like it’s 2002 an’ all. Y’reckon it’s gonna take an hour to get outta this jam?      Look, I appreciate you’re wound up, but I’ve had eenough of you passive-aggressive remarks today. It’s just traffic.      Oh aye? Aye, but I’ve got this project due tomorrow an’ I promised me mate I’d meet ‘em. An’ now me car’s warmin’ up, but me brain’s not. Gettin’ real jumpy, innit?      Alright, calm down. We canitunes that MySpace playlist you like, see if it helps. It’s either that or start playin’ D&D in me head.      Haha, yeah, a bit of The Darkness breakfast, innit? Look, while we’re delayed, I’ve been wonderin’ about this job lot, you know, the corpus admin? It’s quite niche, but I fancy it.      Yeah, I remember you ranted about your exams as if you were supplying the Ministry of Magic with bookshelves.      Well, yeah, got a good batch of – Mate, I got a real interest in how people talk, innit? So, somethin’ to do wi’ that’s cool.      Makes sense, you’ve always had that attention to detail. Although I reckon you could just walk into a building an’ do an accent hotter than the summer sun.      Don’t be so crude! Look, it’s not just accents about how people communicate. I mean, it’s such a different lot of lingo from a posher accent like yours. Proper data to sort out.      True, true. But ‘posher’ is such a funny word. I live in Harpenden, not the White House. But yeah, I can see it being accurate.      We could talk about queens and kings for ages, but traffic ain’t doin’ a new plan while we do.      Still, I’m intrigued. What sort o’ projects are you goin’ on with it? Something academic or more real-world?      It’s a bit of both, actually. Some academic journals an’ virtual assistants. It’s about fluency, innit? Making tech understand us better so it don’t bellyache so much.      Sounds proper progressive. Maybe one day it'll   tell the time so we don’t have to shout at the phone.      10-4, boss! Now, when we get outta this, I swear you won’t get a word in again. C’mon, roundabout’s makin’ a u-turn for us.

Rather a gray day, isn't it? That rain's been drizzling on for hours now. Mind if I put the kettle on? Just about the only way to keep warm in this wretched weather.      Not at all, son. Be as you were. No better cure than a good old cup of tea, I say. Light the fire while you’re about it if you can be arsed. I don’t fancy this damp in my old bones again.      Oh, leave him to it! You know Bernard's got his pride. If it’s too much, he won’t fetch the matches himself, will he? I can stir a fire up like nothing, don’t you worry.      Touché, love. I left the kettle on the hob, didn’t I? Danged thing might whistle itself away before the fire’s even lit if you’re not quick.      Heh, this house’s like a time machine, isn’t it? Only thing missing is a floorboard that leads to the treasure room. I remember when that solicitor came to tell me I had to give up the barn. I nearly wept.      And for good reason. That barn was practically a third of this house before it was all sold off. I remember – Richard used to keep the hens in there, and Harold used to swear the cheapest paint was best for clapped-out things like that place.      Aye, those were the days. Though I always said the barn was structurally unsound. Rusted beams, crumbling stonework. A civil engineer’s nightmare.      That’s all very well, but there’s a bit about tangible history that you don't want just to disappear into the ether. It wasn’t just a barn, luv. It was ours.      Still, we’re not in a time for sentiment. If the waters rise high enough, we’ll all be at the mercy of it. You know how the scientists talk about it now – climate change and all that doom and gloom.      Aye, always trying to find a silver lining. But I do miss the mornings with the birds singing and a fresh cup of tea. Now the weather's got goon all on us.      Just don’t expect me to leave, no matter what. I’ve seen too many homes through the years to forget which one I’m happiest in.      That’s the spirit! And don’t forget, Bernard promised to teach you how to play bridge this winter.

Rather annoying this wet weather isn't it? I was supposed to visit the gardens in Eastbourne last week. I got nowitz from it all. I’m more than a bit fed up with the rain, really. I keep wondering when we'll finally have some decent summer weather.      Aye, I know exactly what you mean. I was hoping to take the lads to the seaside for a bit of family time too. With the way this weather has been playing up, I’ve had to cancel twice already. We’ve been stuck mostly at home playing board games when it's not raining. You'd think the sun would get even a little bit tired of hiding, wouldn't you?      Oh well, you know how it is with the weather here. One day of sunshine, and half the country floods. But I was thinking of something else too. I heard on the radio the other day about this breakfast programme—there was an interview about some new education policies in Scotland. They were talking about revising the curriculum, even looking at teacher training again. Goodness, I hope they treat us with a bit more respect than they used to up there.      Ah, you and the teaching profession. I might’ve known something on that would catch your attention. Be fair, you’ve always been passionate about it. But I agree, it's disgraceful how often teachers are overlooked despite all the hard work and dedication. I have a cousin who still teaches in Fife and she's telling me it feels like the system doesn’t care.      That's just it. You give your life to those kids, and suddenly you're being told you're overpaid or overqualified. Honestly, most people about would fall off their perch trying to do the job the way we do. Not much recognition or thanks—that's part of the reason why I gave it up.      I understand. And I admire you for it. All those years, shaping young minds, trying to do it right. But I think it's very different for me. I haven’t had your kind of pressures, as much as I try to live up to the same standards. I think it helps to have the structure of working in the same school for so long.      Oh, go on then, don’t be modest. If it wasn’t for people like you in the profession, who's going to teach all the rest of the little strays like myself how to read, or to behave, or even to think?

Rather chilly this evening, isn't it? I turned the heating on ages ago, but it's been like a sauna and a shower at the same time today. Blows hot air for ten minutes, then stops and leaves us shivering. I'll have to call someone about it.      Got a problem like that at my place last winter. Turns out the heating engineer had left all the valves half-shut. A complete mess. I got so fed up I bought a log burner. It was easier pulling wood in than waiting for the gas to kick in. Didn’t even want to heat the place properly.      Oh, I envy that. I've been stuck in the lab all week trying to sequence that Mycobacterium sample, and it's left me feeling like I need a nap and five sandwiches. A crackling fire would make a world of difference. But I’m far more worried about Christmas shopping. I haven’t bought a single thing. Honestly, I’m running on mulberries, takeaway, and anxiety.      Mulberries? Good call, those things are wicked when they stain, though. I made a t-shirt last week with some freshly squished ones and now it looks like something out of a gothic horror film. Doesn’t bother me, mind. I find it intriguing. My Christmas plans are mostly about making stuff – I’ve just started a new project with a steampunk twist to sell next year. Should be fun. Bit fiddly with the tools, though. They all seem to be missing!      When it comes to tools, I tend to hoard the lot. You never know when you’ll need a 6mm Allen key in the middle of a storm. I’ve got a whole toolbox you can rummage through if you want. Not much cooking in my world though. I usually eat off a plate and it involves a sandwich, but if you lot are up for it, I’d be happy to learn.      Well, the more the merrier. Do you fancy helping me make something decent for Christmas? I could use the help brainstorming and shopping. I’ve seen mulled wine recipes that include a little brandy and even chocolate, which is… surprisingly brilliant.      That sounds excellent. I can go for a little chocolatey mulled wine. Any chance of discussing retirement at some point? It seems to be coming along, and I’d love to know what everyone’s thinking about post-work life.

Rather annoying that half the cutlery’s missing again. I swear we had more forks last week when we had grandparents and Claire over. Have you seen the spare ones, Mum?      Creator, I don’t know! I’ve been meaning to sort the drawers properly. Andrew keeps taking the good cutlery when he hosts his mates, you know. I reckon his wife's as bad as him. She probably ‘borrows’ things and forgets to return them.      Honestly, someone should invent a system. Like, maybe colour-code the forks or something. That’d at least show whose lot is whose. Still, it’s not like we can complain at the dinner table again. Last time Dad threatened to turkey-baste anyone who mentioned his son-in-law one more time.      Oliver, dear, cut the joking. This is a family evening, for crikey’s sake! We’re all here for a bit of normality, after all. Though I do miss the roasted potatoes M hides behind the gravy boat for the grandchildren.      Dad, you mean the ‘secret stash’?      Aye, well, as long as she’s not hiding them for her book club. I’ve had enough of extra portions in my day. You want meat or –?      Duck, actually. Though I’m not sure the duck survived the kitchen after that squirrel incident. Silly thing darted toward the fridge at ten o’clock.      That’s what I get for leaving the bird food out. I had a squirrel out the other day who looked at me like I’d forgotten their birthday. I swear I heard it mutter, “It about time.”      That’s talking the talk, Jane. Not much else you can say at this age that isn’t dramatic. Still, it does sound like we’re the most popular house for local wildlife. Unless that was a hedgehog.      No, it was a squirrel holding my microwave door with its paws. I had to shoo it out with a tutu. Looked like a ballet performance.      Tutu! Per fi’ the grace o’ you, delivering meals around this t’ble. That was one go’ bin on your life if you ask me.      Thanks, Granda, I’ll take that as a compliment.      Look, all jokes aside, seriously, let’s start sorting the cutlery after dinner. I’m not keen to explain to the in-laws over Xmas why we have a knife missing when they’re coming for dinner.

Rather annoying to be honest, eh? You know what my boss is like.      Yeah... What's the problem?      Blows hot and cold, does he. Had this inquiry pop up with the clients last minute and now he says I've got to come in on Saturday and extend the meeting.      Oh no! That means missing our lesson on Saturday? I've been counting all week!      I know, love. I'm terribly sorry, but it's just business. We'll go for an ice cream when it's over.      Puh-lease! Not when I've been learning to ski, I only want to go and fall on the snow like you did.      Well you haven't told me you've been falling on purpose, and I think I turned out alright. It's all about the resilience!      I know... I just want to go on the big hill with the black circle.      Not for a few weeks yet, poppet. It's still the bunny slope for us until we're properly confident.      What about the other weekend when dad took us? That was a properly good hill.      Be careful what you say. We're trying to get better skiers, not experts overnight.      Yeah, but don't you miss it? Silly glaciers and all.      It’s the chalet that I miss. What a cozy place. You know, they had a log fire and proper mugs of cocoa.      Hey mummy, will we get to stay in a hotel like that in about five days time? I packed my snow man suit already!      You what?      I know! I put it in the packing basket in my room. It had the little hat and everything.      Well that's surprising, but a thoughtful gesture. You know, I might have to take you skiing myself when I sort out this work mess.      Then we can go up the 'black hill' together.      Not quite yet for you, love. But by next season, with the right go at it, we'll be flying down those slopes like proper snow birds. What do you think, will you be the tiniest eagle on the mountain?      I'll be the biggest and best one there, mummy! I promise! You'll see! I can talk to the snowman too!      Well I wouldn't have my daughter any other way, my little ski queen. Now, let's finish our meal so we can make the most of our adventure and our cocoa.
