Rather lovely day today, isn't it? That sun is doin' wonders for the garden. Mind if I put the kettle on? Just about to make a nice pot of tea, like we used to back in Essex.      That'd be brilliant! I wouldn't say no to a cuppa. I've been working from home today, and it's nice to actually sit down properly. Though I've been watching a film to take a break from emails. Have you seen it?      Oh, haven't had the time. You know me — when it comes to films, I'm a bit of a old habit! Mostly rewatching some of the classics, like  Mrs. Miniver  or My Fair Lady. You know, those old ones with a bit of class, not the flashy new ones with too much noise.      Haha, fair enough. I do love an old British film too. I just happened to watch  The Favourite  the other night — it's quite dark, but the performances are so good. Emily Dickinson would probably have given it a pass, if you know what I mean.      Right! Left it to you and the younger generation for that sort of thing. I reckon I'd have been a little lost. Though I must say, I do enjoy a good costume drama. My sister used to watch huge quantities of  Downton Abbey  when it first came out. Still, no insult intended! It's just not the same style.      No offense taken! I get it, different generations, different tastes. Though I’d be lying if I said I didn’t miss some of the witty dialogue from those old movies. Not many about now make me laugh quite the same way the Marx Brothers did.      Exactly! There's a certain charm to that sort of thing. The way they spoke, the way they carried themselves — like proper performers rather than just actors. Although, I did get a kick out of one of your Marvel films once. The one with the spider lad?       Spider-Man: Into the Spider-Verse ? He’s not a lad anymore, more of a laddie, let’s say! It was a great film, very visual, very different from the older stuff I usually see. It's funny, you'd think kids these days would just watch that genre, but I’ve caught myself watching old Doris Day movies at the weekend. Time really does fly!

I can't believe the weather’s better today. That’s a relief. I was starting to worry I’d miss my weekend trip to Stratford-upon-Avon. I’ve got a few days off, and I was hoping to see that new play they’re doing at the Royal Shakespeare Theatre. Has it booked out yet, then? It was all over the telly last week—heap of excitement. You’ve always had a soft spot for Shakespeare, haven’t you? To be fair, it wasn’t just the play. I also need to check out the kids’ school trip to the frozen food warehouse. One of the teachers is driving, but someone said it might rain again. I want to get the turkey stock sorted for dinner too. Ten o'clock on the dot, love. But I thought you were taking the train up to Stratford again? Surely you’re better off breakfasting there than standing at Birmingham New Street with a cup in your hand. That’s what I said to Mum when I told her over dinner last night—settle into the theatre and book a sturdy pint of ale after it’s done. But as it is, I’ve got to iron my blazer. The kids always ask if I’m a Geography teacher again. Oh come on, you’re still smarter than the lot of them. Let’s see… What about that friend of yours at work? The one who’s always at your classes, huh? Remember what someone said in one of the books you read to me? Something like, “It's not what you know, but what you can do with it.”  laughs  You’re quoting Virginia Woolf now. I think I’ll screenshot that the next time she says “crumpet” or whatever. Speaking of, shall I bring some over for tea? I could run to Marks & Spencer, they’ve got proper treacle ones. Aye, sounds grand. I’ll keep the kettle on. Oh, I almost forgot—need your help with the garden. There’s a bit of a mess of a rose bush by the gate, and the cat’s been pinging all over it. The council said if something doesn’t get cut soon, the leaves might go bad. How does ten o'clock sound? I can bring the spades and a cup of strong blooming tea from the train station. It’s all part of the trip to Stratford—save the roses, tea with the cat, then Shakespeare.

Rather annoying that the supermarket’s out of stock on jasmine rice. I was trying to make us that Thai fried rice we liked so much last weekend.      Oh, sure, where are we getting it from? Not the one round the corner again—  Lori   said it was crawling with Chinese students and there  may  or may not be    staff  … not very hygienic.      Why don’t we try the one on   Qingnian road  ? I remember the guy there once gave me free lychee jelly with my shopping. He’s very nice, even if  he is  a bit short and uses a lot of hand gestures.      You mean   Li Yang  ? Oh, I agree, he is sweet—probably stealing glances at you every time you go. Haha, watch out, you’re better than breakfast, apparently.      Haha, yeah, he’s harmless. Listen, we should also pick up those   kombucha cookies   you were craving—did you forget we have a book club this weekend and the last time you had alcohol it turned into a   saxophone solo by the garden gnomes  .      Ugh, no, remember – that was   public mistreatment of inanimate objects   week and the gnomes were injured in the line of duty. Silly British people. Anyway, don’t worry, I’ve already substituted this week’s chicken curry for   quinoa tahini   bites. Trying to be a bit healthier—  you’d be proud.        That’s all  well and good , but your protein intake is still about the same as   a man-eating orchid  . Honestly, if you don’t grow a little muscle I’m going to get   a bit concerned  .      Alright, alright, I promise I will eat a sundae and some pork bao. Compromise? And maybe I can get some of that   lychee balm   while I’m at it. You said it’s supposed to help with that   dry air   from the central heating?      That’s the one. Try not to get lost in the spice section on your own, you always come back with at least one   mysterious powder   that I don’t know how to use.      So I have to stop pretending to speak Thai and just ask out loud? No, never. You can be my interpreter. I like the sound of this walking home—  shop talk,   some banter, all in one. Always forget how good it is to be back in the real world once in a while.      Entirely agree. Let's just pray no one else needs help speaking… this is much safer than my last seminar on postcolonial architecture.

Rather than babysitting the children this evening, I thought we could have the family photoshoot tomorrow morning before they head off to visit Gran in Cambridge. I’m yet to schedule their haircuts, so we might as well do it all in one go. That way, we won't have to juggle it in again during the busy holidays.      But Mummy, tomorrow is the day we read with Grandma Online. A lot of reading tends to happen this week, and Miss Ward said she’d pick some interesting stories to do! Can we still do the photos later in the week, please? The story sessions are my faved part of the school week.      What’s a photoshoot? Can I wear my My Little Pony pyjamas for it though? I like sleeping in them, they’re sparkly, and they pick out the features! They might make my face look less freckled.      A photoshoot is just when we all get in front of the camera for some proper family pictures, you know, for the laptop and the fridge. As for that—yes, we can, but only if it’s not too hot in there, your face might end up looking like a glow stick! And we can read on Friday, how's that? I was also thinking we could bake cupcakes for lunch tomorrow with Gran. I’ve read some recipes for star anise cupcakes online, and she loves those.      If we bake together, can I help mix the batter? Our geography teacher said mixing things is also part of science! And if it counts for that, then can I write about the cupcakes for my science book as an example of a solvolysis reaction?      Of course you can help mix the batter! And the talking part of science is called an ‘explanation’ and not a solvolysis reaction! I’m sure your teacher will be impressed if you mention that ‘you made baked goods’ as part of your topic work. By the way, I’ve also scheduled a surf afternoon with some friends this weekend. It will be your first time out on the water, as long as you feel up for it.      Grasping! I like the sea. My grandad taught me how to shoot tigers! Can I come as go-karts on the coast if you promise not to go over your head? Also, are we having pizza for dinner on Saturday, or something else?

So, I swear the tutorial today was the most utter drivel. I was just doodling through the first half, and I nearly fell asleep. Like, honestly, I can't see how we're supposed to get anything out of this module. Did you even follow what the lecture was about?      Oh dear, I feel you. It was like watching paint dry! My brain actually shut down after a minute. I had to delete like ten of these random social media posts in my head just to stay awake. Honestly, why can't they teach us something useful instead of this, I don't know, abstract nonsense?       laughs  I know, right? I'm only doing this module because my older cousin swears by it, you know, like "you’ll regret it if you don’t do this". But I’m thinking of switching to something more practical. I was at a café gig yesterday and I was like—maybe I just want to be a jazz musician or something!      No, you can’t abandon your degree! Although, I would love that—just vanishing into the night for some music gig. I might take you seriously if your student finance still covered it. For now, I’m just going to be a barista extraordinaire, sipping lattes at my own café one day. I can already picture it!      You’d be great at that! You’ve always been the perfect barista—listening to your customers, making the coffee just right. Oh, by the way, have you tried the new smoothie here? It’s out of this world!      No, not yet! I’ve had such bad fruit smoothie experiences in the past. I once tried a "tropical green" one and it had vibes like a jungle soup. I need someone to vouch for it first. You're up for going to the cinema this weekend for that new comedy everyone's talking about?      Sure, I’ve heard it's hilarious. Do you think we’ll meet up with some other people or just stick to us? I miss that big group of us getting into trouble with lunches and shots.      Let's keep it just you and me for now. We haven’t had a chance to go out really on our own since term started. Think of it as our girls’ day, no drama, no group texts, just laughs and popcorn. Deal?      Deal. But if it's anything like my disastrous trip to the local pub with friends, I'll need backup for when someone challenges me to karaoke again!

Rather annoying I had to cancel me trip to Bath last week. My sister was supposed to take me up first thing, and she ended up no-showin’. Drove my mam up the wall      Aww, honestly that’s rough. Did she at least text you in advance? ’Cause I find that if someone doesn’t even give you a proper heads-up, it's just… not on.      Fair enough. From my point of view, it’s just rude, pulling someone’s leg and then chuckin’ the plan when you're literally halfway there. Still, what else did you have planned, Lucy?      Well the idea was to go up for the weekend and have a look around the Roman Baths. Fun fact’s one of the guides told me was the water in them is still used today in some sort of spa centre. Sounds a bit dodgy to be honest.      That’s not a bit dodgy at all, that’s proper authentic! I mean, if you're going to the hot springs, you’d expect some murky water, wouldn’t you? I’ve been up there once and the whole city is like a giant open-air museum, everything still works there.      Absolutely, it’s got way more charm than some of the new-build places I’ve worked on.      Yeah, but don’t get me started on the new restaurants up there. The one I liked the look of had changed name again since last time. Honestly, they all serve bloody risotto and lemon salmon. It’s all the same!      Hey, risotto is decent food! Look, it’s not rocket science, but at least it’s not turd on toast or whatever this “modern vibes” stuff is that some restaurants cook up. Not that I’d know, I’m more of a takeout and chips ‘til 2 am kind of man      And I prefer to go to cafes where the bloody coffee tastes like coffee, not something you drag out of a spoon after being whipped into a planet.      Precisely! I think it's partly the tourists, too. Too many of em expect something amazing with barely any effort on their part. go in with camera phones and no appetite.      I do not, but that’s aside from the box. Time to change the topic. Speaking of food, have you lot seen the new series of MasterChef?      Oh, I’ve been watching it.

Rather a lot’s been going on, innit? Me and Daisy were just discussing our trip to London. I got the seats sorted out on the train already, and I fancy a few days away where we can see the Tower and all them things. That place in Cornwall frightened me a bit—it gets so foggy and all.      Oh, I remember that youth hostel! It was years ago, but I’ve never forgotten how cold it got in the evenings. Still, we had a right laugh, pulling pranks and everything. Oh, I heard from Edith the other day about the new school up north—they’re saying it’s even older-than-old. I reckon it’s the oldest school still open in the Midlands now.      Old or not, the education is what matters more, ain’t it? D’you know, I bought a second-hand car off an eBay for about a fiver better than I expected—good deal, mind you. Less a bit in rep basins, but it’s a runner, so to speak. Speaking of which, I heard news on the telly—about the election—there’s changes afoot up north in Birmingham, land prices rising like mad. I tell ya, it’s madness buyin' property now.      Speak for yerself, son! I sold me fairly large house in Costessey for a bit more than I hoped. It was a big place for just me, what with no one to cook for. Still, the cash feels good in the tin. Although I’ve not a clue where it all goes.      Just the same with me, dear. Me and Ernie had that bungalow in Harrow, and it nearly did our heads in. I don’t know the likes of today’s property boom. It’s like you could grow capers on the tarmac and get it sold. Still, I like the peace, ‘course. I miss the little lads and lasses when I used to dandle ’em round.      Same, but I’m more into passing on knowledge these days than dandlin’. Though being a teacher is always trying with some of the new whiz-kids today—they’ve got no respect for proper grammar.      Hah! Grammar go out of the window, if you ask me. Just give me a bridle in the hand and I’ll be off with a horse any day. Daisy told me you two were going to watch the match down in Wigan?

Honestly, I don't know how you do it, Em. Every time I think I've got the hang of feeding the baby, she just starts crying again like I've done something wrong.      Oh, don't worry about it, Becca! You'll get the timing down eventually. I'm still fumbling through it most days, and I haven't even gone back to work yet! I feel like I should be halfway to having this under control by now.      You’re doing great! You just have to go with what the baby needs, I suppose. I swear Mine can’t just have enough even if I burp her and everything. What’s your routine like?      Hmm, I feed her on demand most of the time. Probably every couple of hours or so. But I used to stick to the bottle timer method with mine, and that eventually worked better for breakfast, but then she’d just want more frequently after that in the evening. It’s the hardest part, especially with the sleep deprivation.      Wait, who’s that? Come in, come in! Oh, hello, I’m Faye, Becca and Em’s little sister. Just visiting for a few days—it’s been so long since I’ve seen the little one.      Oh, hi Faye! Thanks for coming. This is my new baby, Lola. She’s just over four weeks old. And this is Becca, who’s helping me out with some advice and everything.      Oh, she’s so gorgeous! What made you decide to have her in the UK and not send her to the US with your grandmother, Em?      Honestly, the costs just didn’t make sense, and I didn’t feel safe handing her over that young. Plus, I’d get to see my parents more often to have help, and that made the whole thing less stressful.      I remember when my parents used to pass advice along to me about their sister, you know when I was your age. It was all over the place—some good, some bizarre. I think I once tried feeding my younger cousins with tea. My grandad swore by it.      Oh no! That’s wild! My grandma used to give me real honey in cups when I was a baby, which they say can cause botulism now. But they didn’t know at the time.      Wow, that’s so different from what we have now.

Rather lovely morning, isn't it? I've just made some fresh orange juice for us, if you'd care for a glass. And no, I’m not letting any of you sneak in a Red Bull before breakfast again—Mark, we do remember the chaos that brings!      Thank you, Deborah. That sounds delightful. I think I'll just enjoy the juice and maybe a bit of toast. I’ve got a meeting this afternoon and best be off early to avoid the traffic. It was quite a circus on the A282 yesterday.      Honestly, I think the only reason I woke up early is because my cat decided it was her personal mission to supply breakfast herself. Again! She’s Mycroft, by the way—a name my mother would have found ridiculous. I’m half convinced she thinks stealing toast is how I’ll earn the respect of all the humans in the house.      I’ve been out in the garden this morning—prepared a few beds for the new season. I’m ordering some new flower seeds from the nursery over in Rochester. I think I’ll plant some lilies, they’ve always grown well in this part of the country.      That sounds like a fine idea—Elizabeth, would you like a hand with the planting? I remember my nan used to say lilies brought luck, and they were her pride and joy. Would do well for us to carry that legacy on.      I’d pay good money to hear someone say lilies bring luck. Just trying to decide whether to work from here or the café—truth is, I have a deadline and I want it done early. I’ve had a bit of writer’s block today about this new ad campaign for the coffee shop downtown.      You could always walk and write—you know that bench by the stream near the park does wonders for my thoughts. My father always said the only way he got his best ideas was by walking somewhere and pretending he knew the way home.      I tried that once—I walked in a straight line while lost in thought and ended up in the middle of a duck pond. Rather a cold reception from the caretaker, but it did make for a good laugh around the dinner table later on.      Well, if Elizabeth needs a muse or two, I’m sure we’ll all be here.

I can't believe the midterms are next week already — have you even started revising for maths? Not yet, honestly. I’m more panicking about science, like, where did I put my notes? Do we even know what the chemistry paper will be on yet? Apparently the teacher said something about bonding today, but I completely zoned out — all I heard was a paper plane being thrown by Alex behind me. Honestly, I’m so over studying. It's like, someone just invent a time machine and fast forward to summer! Haha, I get that. I tried revising Art last night, and now I’m just accidentally doodling reindeer in my textbook. Reindeer? Oh no, don't go festive on me now, we're not even halfway through December yet! But hey, I was thinking, since our Christmas break is coming up, maybe we can go into Cambridge after the exams — just a quick wander around the shops and, you know, maybe say hi to the uni ones, they look like they enjoy Christmas more than us! I’d be down for that. We might even find some real cool stamps at that little shop on Trumpington Street. I’ve been collecting vintage ones for ages. My brother says it's “charming, in a slightly odd way.” He’s not wrong, but it's still cool! I got one with a lion on it from the '70s — it looked so ancient! Anyway, what are you going to get your family for Christmas? Well, I thought of getting my mum some orchids — she loves plants, and I’ve been helping her grow a small garden. But I still haven’t got anything for my brother yet. What about you? I’m stuck too! Maybe I’ll do something like Ed Sheeran tickets for them. My gran loves his music — and honestly, I don’t mind hearing it too, it's not like hearing maths revision for 45 minutes again. Haha, fair enough. At least your plan is more fun than my history essay last week. I swear I cried a little. That bad? I still have my pond life presentation to do — about tadpoles and slugs in the pond near our school. Who lives in the sludge, your guess is as good as mine! You’re not helping my mood! I think I’m just going to go on a walk and get over this by looking at green things.

Rather annoying this new rat puppet they've got at the village fayre, if you ask me. Mind you, I rather liked the old bumblebee one. I used to sneak up to see it with my missus before she passed. No, I mean—  what a daft idea for a puppet show!        Oh,   I reckon it depends on your point of view.   I mean, when I was doing the handbell ringing at the chapel, we started off quite crooked as a group. It was like trying to get the run of the mill kids to play nicely together! Not to compare it much, mind—those bells weigh a ton and a half, if you know what I mean.      Ha! Yeah, I remember when you told me about the time the rope broke and nearly hit the vicar! But to be honest, handbell ringing sounds better than breakfast on a bus if you ask me. I had to be driven across town the other day and the driver told me to move near the front so the conductor could see I’d paid. I said, "Excuse me, sir, I have a full plate of pain-free travel and patriotism and I'd like to keep it."      Ah, yes, travel. You’re bound to see all sorts of sights on a bus these days. Though I must say, the cheapest way of getting about these days is through the optician! I went in for a quick check, and the next thing you know, I’m looking at a new pair of tinted spectacles that cost a week’s rationing!      Oh   dear, I feel for you.   I've had my about five pairs in the last decade! And the doctor always says, “Mrs. Harrow, you really must start wearing them all the time or you'll lose your sight.” I say, “Doctor,   if I keep squinting toward the future, perhaps that’s the reason I don’t see a thing coming my way!”        Haha, well, you've got your sense of humour. And your eyesight with it, I s’pose! Speaking of which, you two ought to try a spot of handbell ringing! I mean, even go as far as to see if you can raise a ruckus with the rat puppet, no pun intended.      A ruckus with a puppet?   I might just manage that, though I think I'm more of a puppeteer of people myself.

Rather annoying I know, innit? You’d think they’d get the gist after a few ‘Could ye...’ and ‘If ye don’t mind...’ comments. Not a bad atmosphere though, gotta say. Gonna hit the Rialto Market later, mind if I pick up a few souvenirs een?      Souvenirs again? Ay, I’m all for it, but you’ve got a trunk full from the last trip. Still, what can I say, innit? You’ve got a mind to spend your student cash on trinkets, so who am I to argue? Right, I were thinkin’—what were we gonna do this afternoon, then?      Dunno, I was gonna skive off and find one of them little cafés off the main square, pick up a spritz and just sit an hour in the sun. Mums better not breakfast, innit? I’ve been workin’ on that essay all mornin’.      A spritz and a sunspot, ay?Sounds like you and your gran, luv. I remember when Venice was riddled with cobblestones and you had to step real careful where you put yer foot… plus, the ferries were a little less packed. Used to be a proper town of gondoliers and old artisans, not all these tourists snapping photos and blocking the way to the next stall.      Nah, that’d bore me. Like, someone said Venice was dying ten years ago. Yet here it is, still oddly alive. You ever think about the food? It's like nowhere else here—tiny little restaurants where the owner’s also the waiter and the cook. I’m walkin’ past a place now that’s got this sea bass and polenta special. Smells wicked.      Aye, the food’s the lot, innit? Poached cod with leeks and saffron. I used to go there every Sunday when I was workin’ as a midwife. Not that I was tourin’, mind you—just that one of the lady midwives from London were on holiday and I was coverin’. Some of the best fish I’ve ever had. You’d like it, love.      Honestly, you talkin’ like that makes me want to chuck the essay and head straight down the road to that place now. Pass the sugar, innit.      You eat first, then write your essay. Just like your old mum’s expectin’ ye to over this bloody geography degree o’ yours. I’m not makin’ Arry proud if you come back with another softie of a graduate who can’t peel a potato.

So did you go to the gym this weekend? I remember you saying something about it last week.      Yeah, I went on Sunday. It was so good to actually stick to my routine this time. I think the holidays finally caught up with me!      Me too! I didn't go last weekend at all. Rachel and I went out for a night in Cambridge on a Thursday. A lot of wine and far too many kebabs. Not exactly a healthy start to the week.      That sounds like me during the holidays too. I went to Nandos three times! Still, at least I've been back at the gym, right?      True, you seem to have found your rhythm. It’s just that I’m working on this new project, and it’s been eating up my time. It doesn't help that our deadlines have been pushed forward.      Ugh, I feel that. I'm also swamped at Bupa right now. Marketing a new health service is more complicated than I expected. But hey, maybe we can meet up for coffee next week instead of going to the gym? It might be easier on my schedule.      Sounds like a good idea. I need to take a break from spreadsheets at some point, and catching up with you is always a good pick-me-up.      Definitely. Speaking of picking me up, how are you doing after everything with Mark?      Honestly? I’m healing, but it’s definitely not easy. We’d been dating for a while, and it’s surprising how much energy something like that can take out of you.      I’m really sorry, Jess. I had something similar a few months ago. Time does help, but it's not like it fades overnight. You’re not alone, though.      Thanks. I know. I just have to focus on my growth and not let the past define my future.      That’s the spirit! So what about your plans after work? Any big moves or exciting holiday plans coming up?      I think I might take a solo travel trip later this year. Maybe go to Portugal on my own if I save enough. Just something different, you know?      That sounds amazing! You’ll have your own virtual diary to update me with, right?      Of course! And maybe even some photos from Nandos in Lisbon for nostalgia's sake.      I’m in! Let’s make it happen and keep our health and crazy adventures in balance, one Nando's at a time.

Rather exciting to be called grandparent, isn't it? I still can't believe it's real. Born in France, you say? Just imagine, they're already learning two languages by immersion! A bit of a cultural switch from Stratford, don't you think?      Aye, it's beginning to sink in, more so with the letter from Margaret this morning. I've been thinking a lot lately about France since I'm working on that new project. The countryside, you know, land, property—absolutely labyrinthine to the outsider. You can't chase enterprise without meeting the bureaucrats at every step, like they're guarding some ancient family secret.      I heard only last week about an anarchist organisation in Paris protesting against city planning! The French have flair, even when they're agitating for their causes. But I was sad to read the news about Chichester Cathedral’s spire collapsing. Such a shame—do you recall the architect’s name? I believe he was a Mr. Porden.      Yes, Porden. Good chap, built that spire over 300 feet, sturdy as they come. I remember visiting the cathedral as a lad. I tell you, when I did my archival research on Philip of Spain and Mary Tudor, I found so much at the British Library: writings from Spanish archives and letters that had never been translated. One letter almost setPhilip of Spain and Mary Tudor’s affairs alight in my head! Makes you wonder what kind of buried histories still lie waiting for someone with a notepad.      I do wonder what you'll do with it all in the end. Any chance I could preview a chapter when it’s done? I have about five bollards' worth of story to share here: had this great debate at a local housing open day about their lack of open days themselves and housing issues. No one mentioned photographers, but there was talk of an art competition guest speaker expressing more enthusiasm about concrete slabs than open spaces.      Ah, the art world—their enthusiasm for dull things always makes me crack a smile. But I’ll tell you what—when I visited that exhibition a couple of years ago in Chichester, it was like stepping into something from my book. Visuals can tell as much history as the best-vetted academic material.      You're always making connections between history and the everyday, old friend. I can't blame you.

I can't believe the naan bread here isn't even edible. My sister had her fill of real Indian food when we went to Manchester last year. This stuff tastes like cardboard! Haha, I know right? We ordered spring rolls and they were basically just rice paper wrapped around soggy veggies. My friend went there last week and told me the same thing. Honestly, I don't know why my cousin picked this place. Slough's got tonnes of better Indian restaurants. She probably just wanted somewhere we all knew. I mean, most of us are into the same things anyway — comics, school jokes, even united over bad food. I swear we could write a comic called "The Lunchtime Fiasco." Just four teens surviving restaurant hell! That sounds awesome, I’d read it! But for real, school has been so nuts lately. I’ve got GCSE mocks coming up, and I’m already stressing about them like a total lunatic. When’s the last time you lot even ate anything not pizza or chips? Last week I had salad, if you can believe it. My mum got tired of me eating the same thing and made me try real food. I tried to make a funny out of it by texting my friends like “rejecting fast food – trending soon.” But no one laughed. Honestly, the only thing trending in our class is how many phone messages people are deleting when the teacher walks by. Like, I saw this one girl in Year 10 with a conspiracy theory about the teacher being an alien. Wait, really? What’s next? The teacher is using mind-control to get us to revise? I about blocked out my essay on the Cold War the other week — had to re-read it like five times and even then it wasn’t that good. Maybe we’re all just rebelling against the system. My little brother started drawing superhero comics based on our teachers. Mr. Johnson is a time-traveling librarian with a laser beard. That’s genius! Why not publish it as a joke zine or something? We could call it "Year 11: The Class Defiance Chronicles." You know, it could go on the website or go viral on one of those social media apps everyone uses now. Imagine making that into a group project with our media studies class. Pass off creativity as homework — win-win.

Rather annoying this new supermarket’s branding, isn't it, Sarah? I was in there yesterday and it felt more like a conference centre than a place to buy your tea and scones.      Aye, we do see the same thing up at the school. The kids make jokes about it—standing there with their trolleys twitching like they’re about to deliver a presentation. Though I suppose it is a bit posher than the old one.      It's not like it’s a library or sommat. You're just chase shopping, innit? I mean, I like the branding—it looks like  Instagram . My mates say we need to go there for brunch on the weekend and MySpace it all up.      Honestly, branding is the least of their worries. We're halfway through clearing out the house for the move, and I’ve found at least six breakfast cereals from the '70s still in the cupboard. No wonder the kids think we lead nomadic, indulgent lifestyles.      That’s not surprising—when we were your age, we rationed the occasional rusk with enthusiasm! Still, I must say the idea of redecorating is exciting… although I’ve decided to keep my little potted geraniums—they’ve watched three generations grow.      You and your plants, Joyce! Now don’t go making them the centrepieces at the birthday event. We’ve been planning something for Jonathan this weekend at the new house—thought maybe a low-key garden party, weather permitting. Would you all be about to help?      Er, sure—I mean, it’s not like I’ve got about five GCSEs to revise or anything. Though can we get a speaker going? I’ve already found some old iPhone that might plug in.      You’re not using a ‘speaker’—I’ll bring in my speaker system. Just don’t play too much trap music—Joyce was quite shocked last time I tried to sync a little Armin van Buuren to our move.      He knows the '70s were better! Now, if we're all going for this bash, I’ve made some rhubarb crumble. Mabel gave me a bag full of it, so I fancied a bit of baking. Hopefully, it'll go with the vibe.      Ah yes, the crumble—the national dish of the north, n'est-ce pas? Just don’t go making it into a ‘wellness’ thing, like they do with everything these days. Served best with a little cold milk and a good cackle at the state of the internet, in my opinion.

So, have you decided yet what GCSEs you're going to take? I'm still stuck on like... art and geography, but my mummy keeps pressin' me to do triple science. It's mad, innit?      Honestly, I wouldn't worry too much. I just signed up for English, Maths, Biology, and PE. My form teacher's all "You should do triple sci, it opens up more job opportunities later," but honestly, I'm more into music. I think clarinet might be my thing long-term.      Oh, you play too? That’s epic! I mostly listen to bogs and bloggers online to keep up with stuff. There's this one YouTuber, Zaynab, she’s like this uni student, but she does these GCSE vlogs and I think I'm just gonna watch her for now.      Ooh yeah, I've heard of her! I prefer Joanne Blo’s stuff, though. She's got this massive following and helps people with uni prep, too. I mean, do you even know what you want to be when you finish school yet?      Not really, to be honest. I like watching shows about proper job stuff, like Dragon’s Den. I think being a content creator could be cool, like, making videos or something. Although, my teacher said I need to pick something "reliable." Like, who knows what will be reliable in 10 years?      Fair point. I reckon it's all about following your passion, really. Also, have you seen the way Taylor Swift’s rep is using all that social media stuff now? Kinda about time rich people finally start acting normal.      Don't get me started. My little sister is obsessed with her new era and it's a bit much. I do think, like, the way she's managing her brand is kinda inspiring. Though I’m not sure if it's a life I want to lead. I dunno, maybe waiting till I’m older.      Right. And also, trying to do perfect duty in school is literally the worst. My head of year keeps calling me out for not tucking in the dinner lady's goody bin on time. I'm like, seriously, give me a trophy just for showing up, will you?      Haha, totally. PE is the only time I don’t want to leave my seat. Why do they think doing burpees is fun?      Yeah, why not yoga or dancing like a normal person?

Rather a dreary day in Norfolk, isn't it? I've been trying to get my old laptop sorted—ever since I upgraded to Windows 10, it's been a right pain. It keeps crashing when I try to run the old programs I used for designing things back in the day.      Aye, I understand that one very well. I tried getting my grandson to help me with a tablet last week—he just gave me the side eye and said, “Grandad, you can't dump spreadsheets onto a phone!” I said, “I never did when I was your age!”      Bless you both! I still can't get my head around all that clicking and swiping. I'm more of a pen and paper woman. Though I must say, I do love the photos I've been taking of the birds I see in the garden. Living in Harrow, there wasn't nearly so much wildlife—this place has proper robins and woodpeckers!      You lot never cease to amaze me. I still remember when I was starting out as a lecturer, you all had to write everything by hand. I showed my students a video from the early 80s where someone tried to draw a parabola using a software program, and they couldn’t believe how clunky it looked with all those jagged lines.      Aye, and don’t get me started on the cars these days. When I was at work, we used to rely on someone who could actually get under the bonnet and fix a problem without needing a diagnostics tablet. Some of them modern motors have more computer chips than a radio!      That’s the truth! Not long about, I popped down to the garage trying to get the misfiring fixed on my old Ford. The lad behind the desk plug it in and goes, “Right, we’re going to need ‘cosy up’ for a couple weeks.” I said, “That’s not a diagnostic it’s a telephone call, love!”      I remember when I was a childminder, and I had to take a young lad who’d recently moved from the countryside with his parents. He ran about the house shouting, “There's no birds here! Where’s the blue tit that chased my pond?” I chuckled and said, “And what made you think we’d got that far up in the box rooms?”      Ha! You all have the best stories.

Rather annoying the new schoolteachers these days, ain’t they? I was speaking to my niece ‘n’ she says the kids don’t even know the times tables by heart! Back in my day, we had to learn them off parrot or we didn’t get our pudding.  Grins . Although, I een’t the sort who likes to say one thing 'bout schools if I don’t know the other, mind.      Oh Charles, this isn’t funny! You’d think education was some sort of joke. We need to teach the children respect, not chase after them with sweets. But mind you...  laughs ... even I used to sneak a fag round the back of the school when I was a teenager. Though I suppose that was more ‘bout the wardrobe fitting than the lessons, to be honest.      I think school has changed a lot, actually, far more than you’re giving it credit for. The kids I taught were bright alright — in their own way, at least. There’s just more to deal with now — drug taking, mental health, that sort of thing.      Mental health, ha! I never heard anything quite as tosh as that. If you’ve got a problem, you walk it off or work it out with a good laugh. Though I must say, I got a real chuckle from that joke the delivery man told the other day — don’t remember it now, but it was something to do with a chicken and the NHS.      Oh yes, the delivery men: they’re a character bunch. I had a one with a chuckle who wore a red trilby and told me he used to tweet when he was younger because he thought about things twice as much back then!  Snorts .      I suppose you could say he was wasting data then! I mean, if you're going to binge drink and tweet at the same time, you're hardly expressing much thought, are you?       Chuckles  Well said Terry. I tried binge drinking once when I was younger and ended up in A and E after being clumsy with a chair.  Pauses . That was one of the few times the health service gave me proper attention.      Oh, the health service is a beast of a system sometimes. If it wasn’t for the nurses and the smiling cleaning staff, I’d go mad in that place.      The NHS is the real hero, really.

Blimey, this snow’s better than a proper Sunday roast! I haven’t seen it this heavy in Sunderland since I was a nipper. You reckon it’ll clear up by tomorrow, or we’ll have to borrow me Ma’s £20 ceramic shovel again? If it keeps up, we might not clear it  at all —just dig ourselves a den! But seriously, we need to grab the ladder and de-ice the greenhouse. If those tomatoes are gonna see the light of day, they ain’t going to grow in the dark under twelve inches of slush, are they? Right, I’ll get Mary to borrow Mrs. Jenkins’ ladder. She’s still got her on about that posh turkey curry from the last Come Dine With Me we tried. Probably gon’ show up with a lemon tart and a judging eyebrow. Think we should warn her she’s about to be eaten by snow drifts? Fair’s fair, but only if she helps us clear the path! Speaking of, have you picked the venue for the stag do yet? I fancied one of those big barn conversions, y’know the ones in the countryside with a real ale and a few hairy jokes? Told John we’d do something quirky this time. Suggesting a competitive knife-throwing with a keg and some bunting. Got a hen-do idea somethin’ to do with spa days and a surprise goat yoga session. Smashing the patriarchy one bamboo mat at a time. That sounds like a nightmare of glitter and sourdough— you’d  have a nightmare with real goats being calm. Can we promise  no ballet sessions ? Last time I did ballet I broke a heel and a man’s eardrum at the same time. Done. But seriously, I’ve got it all sorted up for the hens. What ‘bout the blokes’ guest list? Need to warn Simon his jokes aren’t going to go down if any ‘of us are chuckin’ forks. Aye. As for the holidays… I’ve been eyeing up a tiny cabin near Keswick. More rocks than fiesta, but no ghastly tourist tarts with tongs and man-buns cruising go-karts on pond life. Think our tomatoes could go with us as a plant-based souvenir? You’re bloomin’ mad. But yes. Tomatoes and pesto in the Lake District—sure, why not? Just so long as we don’t meet a third of the village with ‘plants over pronouns’ written on their teacups.

Rather lovely to have you all under one roof, what with it being ages since we had such a proper family meal. I've been chucking a few rhubarb crumbles into the oven after dinner — a little taste of spring, don’t you think?      Oh, Frank, that een't the sort of treat we see often ‘nuff these days! My George used to say rhubarb was only fit for pigs, but I always said, nonsense! Warm with custard and a bit of brown sugar—ah, now that’s what I call a proper elevenses.      That actually makes me think, Dad—last week I was teaching the Year 12s about British culinary traditions and you know, I was surprised how few of them could even name more than fish and chips as traditional food! Frank, I think you ought to be teaching a class, not just baking!      Heh, I mean, with a bit of repackaging, you could totally monetise this, Frank. Rhubarb crumble masterclasses, or even a booklet—Frank’s Rhubarb Wisdom or whatever—there are plenty of people out there who’ve never had a real one, let alone tried making it.      Well, then, I best start taking bookings for that cookbook of mine. I’ve still got that plum cake recipe up my sleeve, and the apple pie that never cracks the crust. If I’m ‘fixin’ to become a foodie in this here kitchen, then I’ll need to audition my best ones tonight.      Oh, yes, and don’t skimp on the anecdotes, Frank! The stories make it all the better. Like when I first tried your steak pie all those years ago and the gravy ran down my chin and I couldn’t stop crying because it was that good! George nearly fell off his chair laughing.      That’s the kind of tradition we should passed on, really. Cooking isn't just about the recipe; it's about bringing people together, hearing stories, remembering things. I could see us doing a session over at the community centre, you know, with lunches and a little history with the meals.      And let’s not forget the best bit—which is all of us goin’ on for hours about our taste memories. Just imagine it—Frank line in, Catherine’s stories, and the three blokes arguing over what ‘proper gravy’ really is.      You lot, I'm startin' to think we might be born to feed the world, ‘nstead o’ just ourselves.

Rather annoying that the oven’s on the blink again, isn’t it? I was trying to whip up a casserole before coming over.      Not a problem, we’ll just use the grill in the kitchen. I’ve seen your mum use it for everything.      That’s my favorite, the grill. Not like these fancy ovens today—they all break down on a rainy day. Back when I was your age, I used to cook for ten people on a single flame.      I preferred just heating up a tin, myself. Still do, specially now that I’ve got all the time in the world.      That’s quite the upgrade from working turkey shifts, isn’t it?      Probably, but I’d rather not risk getting pickled in the sunlight again.      Back in my day, breakfast, dinner—same thing. Just some stew or bread in the larder.      We do have a bit of that, actually, under that stale bread over there. Might have had some company in it.      Left to itself, and only for special occasions.      Well, we’ve been lucky. This house is so much prettier than when we were younger, and way bigger than mine and Anna’s first flat.      You always were a lucky one, didn’t you? Still, better than living out someone else’s skyline.      I wish I thought like that when I was renting that crate out near Peterborough. Half the roof blew off one night.      Sounds like about half the place.      That’s how I used to live out in the northwest. Going into Manchester was like entering a different country.      My parents had that little story about the guest coming in and knocking a glass off the shelf.      Oh yes, the very one—the way you told it, I could see the glass clear as day.      Mum, do you keep the recipe book tucked in the drawer under the sink? Still trying to find it.      Of course, it’s right there if you don’t mind the odd spider or two.      Honestly, with all the stories and the house, it’s like we have our own little corner of history in one room.      You could say that. Just don’t fall for the floorboards when you step them.      Unless I trip, and they come right up with me.      Right place, right people. Better than anywhere else I used to be.      And better still with some fresh cake out of my last batch, once we’re done.

So do you remember that time we worked on that start-up back in Wellington? I think it's time we brought some of those ideas back into the educational system, don’t you think? Especially now, with universities being so starved for funding and students feeling like they're just going through the motions.      I do, yeah. It was one of those projects that almost got off the ground before it even hit the air. I think your presentation got too much social media attention; it went viral and then got pulled back. We had to shut it down for legal reasons. But, come on, you know I’ve always believed in your vision.      Yeah, the video accidentally leaked another company's IP. It was a nightmare. But back to the universities. I’ve been thinking – what if we integrated co-created learning spaces, and brought in more entrepreneurial experiences? Like, students could pitch ideas and get mentorship while still earning college credits.      That could work. Imagine combining business and education in one space, even at the university level? It might actually attract more international students. I spoke to some colleagues at Dorchester campus—there are plenty of frustrations about the disconnect between theory and real-world application.      Exactly. And what if we used a blended learning approach? Think about using some of the viral video content we’ve seen, but repurposed as educational tools. Podcast-like formats for problem-solving assignments? Maybe even gamify some of the assessments? It’d keep students engaged in a way that traditional essays never could.      Gamification is oddly undervalued in higher education, don’t you think? I’d be happy to run a prototype through one of my teaching modules. I’ve got a group of post-grads from all over the world this term. They might be perfect for testing this out. But you’re going to handle the business side, right? I’m not quite overcoding the development plan part.      Of course, that’s the whole reason I mentioned this. I can reach out to some investors I met at a conference in Sydney last month—there was a lot of buzz around ed-tech firms recently. I think we could spin this into a company, maybe even set it up as a not-for-profit at the start to get govt backing on board.      Just don’t expect me to be the face of the pitch.

I can't believe it's already Friday! You know what that means—tomorrow's the weekend. Have you got any plans beyond surviving Thursday's chaos? I'm thinking I might need something like a takeaway and a movie marathon. No, I haven't! Thursday was wild at work—I had three patients in the morning, and then the clinic was slammed. I think I just need to relax completely on Saturday. Maybe I'll just sleep until noon and then maybe whip up a roast? Do you want to join me? A roast sounds amazing! Didn’t your mum teach you how to make that wonderfully chunky gravy last time you visited her? I still haven't perfected it, only managing to make something like watered-down syrup. You're my best hope left for a decent Sunday lunch. Darcy, that was sad. Very sad gravy. I will save you by sharing the family recipe. I still miss Bucks though; I mean, returning after all this time and being back in the Chilterns, you know? I keep thinking I’ll end up in Bedfordshire by accident one day. I know what you mean! I keep telling myself one day I’ll move to Hertfordshire or something. Just watching shows set in the countryside and then being like “Okay, maybe my life is too urban.” I almost applied for that project coordinator role in York. You know, trying to escape the chaos and phone calls of London. York? That’s a big change. I think it could be amazing for you. Working remotely is easier than we ever thought. I’m still looking at some continued education though—maybe a weekend module at King’s or something in London. You know I love crises as much as I love coffee. Oh come on, you thrive on chaos and not coffee alike. But you’re right, it is a good time to step up your game. And hey, if you do go full professional nurse, you can just have me on the list of your patients when my pottery class disaster relapse strikes. Ha! Noted. Now, about Halloween—anything planned? Because I've already got a little party with friends in Greenwich if you're in. Still trying to get a nice tiki torch vibe going, even in the flat on the fourth floor. Yes! I'm just in the middle of figuring out a costume.

Rather chilly this morning, isn't it? I needed six cups of tea just to get out of bed. I remember the days when I could leap up at dawn and go for a brisk walk without a second thought. Seems like my legs have other ideas these days.      Honestly, I don’t get how you can drink six cups of tea in the morning. I manage with one—black, with a bit of milk—and I'm set for the day. I’m so used to rushing into work, there's no time to slow down anyway. Cambridge is always so peaceful when I come over, though.      It is, isn’t it? I love having the garden all to myself. Quiet and serene. My birds are quite the early risers though—they start a right racket! I made some scones yesterday, by the way. A bit heavy for your taste, perhaps, but Mummy’s recipe. I thought we could have a proper Anglo meal after your last takeaway curry!      That sounds perfect to be honest. I could do with something more homely—especially after the long week I had. I’ve been up since 5 a.m. sorting out shipments and supplying the printers, it feels like there's never a quiet moment.      That does sound relentless. You should take more breaks. I know you're swamped, but you are the one managing the whole thing, aren’t you?      I am! It's a case of 'sort it out yourself' for the most part. I had a rush order for some textiles a week ago and had to reshuffle my entire schedule. It was frantic. That said, I did get a good review at the end of the month—supposed to be the next step up, finally.      Oh! That is excellent news. I've always known you're capable, but to have your work acknowledged like that—well, that’s something to be proud of. I’m so happy for you, love. What do you think you’ll do once you’ve had that break you so desperately need?      I'm thinking of taking a proper holiday. Maybe somewhere with less hustle and more ‘aha’ moments—like a countryside retreat with good books and the odd cup of goon. I might even take you up on your scones.      I’d be delighted. That blooming bird song might drive some people mad, but I think I’ll manage.

Rather annoying this wet weather innit? You’d think in France they’d know how to do summat abou’ the rain!      Blows! I thought summer would mean sunshine, but it’s more like we’re in the middle of a monsoon. Have you been checking uni info yets?      Yeah, I’ve looked at a few places. Doncaster’s a bit far from any decent universities tho. D’ya think I should stretch and go further, or just stick to somewhere local?      If it’s worth the coursework and the vibe, I’d go further. I’m still dead excited tho, cambridge’s got some proper cool courses and like actual scientists working on proper inventions!      Right, well I’m not obsessed with research, maybe more of the applied stuff. I fancy teaching secondary actually, but uni doesn’t seem like breakfast, no Bucks Fizz this time!      Blooming mad, but fair enough, you’d be good at it. Are you gonna need help with the application? I can translate a bit for you too—someuni websites are a bit thick in their native language and all.      Oh brilliant, I tried reading it in French but got more confused. My brother works as a translator but I wouldn’t bother him for this!      It’s fine, I can help. Oh, have you heard Liam Gallagher’s been on the radio lately? someone at uni said his new album is barking mad.      Oh yeah, I’d skipped it. I like real music still—ya know, like  Arctic Monkeys  or  Drenge . Not a fan of all the touchy-feely stuff.      Yeah, sorry that’s not really my taste either. I’d sooner listen to some prog, like  Porcupine Tree . But hey, to each their own.      Sure. Oh, scientists say there’s a way you can measure how plants react to light by measuring oxygen levels. Isn’t that barking mad?      More barking mad? We’ve got that in Cambridge, something to do with chlorophyl and leaves acting goenvironmental on us. I think it’s called photosynthesis!      Oh yeah, we done that in school. I remember one experiment where you measured how much oxygen came off a weed and then you graphed it. Properly proper methods for it all.      Sounds proper mad. I’d struggle to measure that. You’d go all over the place if they gave me an actual experiment.      Right, you’d probably make a mess and then want a flippin’ coffee before scribbling anything!

I swear, I saw a spider the size of a coin in our garden the other day! It was absolutely enormous. Ah, you British lot always make a mountain out of a molehill! I see spiders that big all the time. They’re harmless as long as you leave them be. I know, I know. It was just so big and hairy. Almost as if it had a life of its own, scurrying around under the shed. It was probably a woodlouse spider. They’re quite common and pretty good at keeping the woodlice population under control. That’s actually a relief. I was beginning to think we had an infestation on our hands! You probably did. Spiders themselves are infestations, but if they’re keeping other creepy crawlies at bay, you might just thank them in the long run. Hmm, fair enough. I mean, they do their own kind of cleaning, you could say! Speaking of, have you ever seen the mice that come through the walls in the winter? Oh, I’ve dealt with them plenty of times. You can always tell when it’s started getting cold. They go on a rampage for warmth and food. It's relentless at my house. I’ve tried traps, and even that natural remedy with the ultrasonic ones. Nothing quite works. You know what works best? Traps with peanut butter and some old newspaper. Let the mice get used to the smell before setting the trap. That’s a good point. I haven’t tried that. Any word on whether they actually make a dent in the problem or if about five traps just walk away empty every time? You have to be a bit patient and maybe place them near any small gaps or cracks around the house. Those are their secret highways, believe me! I will definitely give it a shot. On a lighter note, do you have birds in your garden? I tried to attract some little ones with birdfeeders, but they just end up being constant warfare zones! Yeah, it's funny how birds regulate the ecosystem in their own way. You put out some food and the blue tits come goading all the others. Exactly! I end up watching the feeding frenzy more than I do eating my breakfast. Maybe try a suet block. They can hold up against the weather and it tends to bring in all sorts of different birds.

I can't believe we've never met before. I suppose family history tends to take a back seat when everyone's busy with their own lives. But it's comforting to find we have a few connections after all. Oh, quite! I've always been curious about our shared surname—it's funny how it appeared in different parts of the country. My late husband used to dabble in family trees, you know. He might have found your side of the story fascinating. My mother was quite meticulous about her documents. She kept extensive records of our family history. Unfortunately, she passed away last year after a long battle with Alzheimer's. It was incredibly hard. I've been trying to go through her things since then. I’m so sorry for your loss. It’s a cruel disease, Alzheimer's. I lost my dear friend’s mum to the same condition—watching someone fade away like that is truly heartbreaking. Did your mother work much in her later years? Yes, she was a school librarian, much like many of the women in her generation. She worked until she was 65 and had a passion for literature and learning. I think that's one of the reasons I became a teacher. I wanted to share that same joy of discovery with students. That's lovely. I taught primary school for forty years and found that nurturing curiosity in young minds was one of the greatest joys of my career. Silly as it might sound, I still keep in touch with some of my former students. Some of them even visit me from time to time. That’s wonderful. I'd love to hear more stories from your time in teaching—I’ve always admired those who dedicate their lives to education. I'm currently teaching English to Key Stage 3 students, but I've thought a lot lately about expanding my role into something more academic or historical, especially after going through my mother’s papers. If you're interested in history, why not branch out? I used to collect historical anecdotes for my lessons—they always brought a spark to the classroom. I remember once reading about my own grandmother and how she survived the Bristol Blitz. It was a story I shared with the children every year, and it brought history to life for them. That’s brilliant advice.

I can't believe we've never done this before. This countryside walk is absolutely stunning. Do you think we could stay here and go camping this weekend? I'd love that. I saw a spot by the river where we can set up the tent. But first, wouldn't you like to visit that nearby balloon event they mentioned last week? Yes, it sounds wonderful! Though I'm a bit nervous about all the machinery and the power lines I saw on the map. I just don't know if it's safe. You're right to be cautious. But I think the event site is far enough away from any major lines. I'll double-check the details, don't worry. Thanks, love. I just get worried around high tension lines. They always look so... dangerous, even from a distance. I get you. For now, let's just enjoy our walk. I love how this path winds through the wheat fields. It's like being in a painting. I know! And look, over there, that fox! I haven't seen one for ages. Lucy would be so excited if we ever saw one with her dogs. Tell me about it. Lucy always wants to bring her dogs when we go out. Though I'm not sure they'd be too happy with hot air balloons either. Definitely not. All that noise and the bright colours would make them go crazy. Still, the wildlife is incredible in this area. We're lucky to live near all this. I know. It’s one of the reasons I chose this job over the university in London. The peace here is exactly what we need. I agree. And you can't beat the salary we're earning here. I know some of my sister's friends are struggling with the cost of living in the city. Yeah, the cost here is much more manageable. Although, with that comes the challenge of the minimal facilities. But overall, it's worth it. Absolutely. I just hope Lucy doesn't mind that we're doing a lot of walking with lunches on a blanket instead of going out to cafes every weekend. I think she understands. She's into the outdoors as well. Plus, it's more cost-effective, and at the camping event, we can do that together. And maybe, if the balloons are on, we'll invite her and the dogs over.

I can't believe how lovely it's been lately. I remember being outside the other day, and it felt like spring had finally arrived. Don't you think it's perfect weather for a gym class after? Aye, can't argue with that. It's a far cry from the frost we had during January. Still, I don't complain - as long as we're getting people in the gym, I'm happy. What with managing this lot in this chain, every sunny day is a bonus. I can imagine. My classes are going pretty well, though, don't get me wrong. I teach Spanish at a local school. People are always surprised to learn the different expressions associated with the weather in other languages. Oh, you must have heard the one about Spain, "Llueve a cántaros." Fair enough - I suppose if it was raining harder than buckets dropping, I'd call it bucket rain too. Exactly! Language is usually tied to culture and experiences, you know? I've always been fascinated by that. I actually did a postgraduate module on multilingualism and education - really opened my eyes. Sounds interesting. I took a course as well, on management - not quite as exotic, I know. But it's helped me improve how I coach new team members, and how I interact with gym members. People respond well to clear communication and positive feedback. Absolutely, and you can see the principles carry over in different situations. Spoken language also has a role to play in bonding and building trust. I remember working with a student who was a bit shy, and being able to use their first language to welcome them made a big difference. That's impressive. I've always found it difficult to grasp a whole new language. My sister is fluent in French and I've never managed a word. I'd quite like to give it a go though, maybe start with some simple greetings. That's a great idea. I think it's very empowering to be able to understand and communicate in another language, even if it's just to say hello or order a croissant. I can recommend a couple of resources if you'd like. That'd be helpful, thanks. I reckon goin' on your own about it's not much fun. Gotta have someone to motivate you, you know. Speaking of, have you been to your usual café near the tennis club in Solihull?

Rather chilly this mornin', innit? Thought me ‘n the missus’d pop ‘round first thing wi’ a spot o’ tea an’ a few scones for you two. Thought we could make a day o’ it. Look like we’ve got a bit o’ weather coming in again een t’afternoon, so best make the most o’ the nice bits.      Aye, thanks, Gran! That’d be brill. The weather’s a bit of a wobbler today. We’ve been stuck inside most of the week. Just wantin’ somethin’ different. You sort of baked scones? I thought you’d forgotten how after all these years.      Oh, bless yer! I might not ‘ave much left up ‘ere, luv, but pastry is one thing I’ll never lose. Back in Hull, I’ve been known to make breakfasts for the whole street if they were stuck in for a bad week. I charmed ‘em all, you know, wi’ a scone an’ a bit o’ jam.      Aye, an’ I’d be the one stuck in the corner, supplying the tea, since I’m no good at domestic matters. But by George, when it got to the loo – that’s where I could help, and I made myself indispensable there too. Let’s say the scones were your moment, Lil. I dealt wi’ the waste.      Haha, now there’s a good ‘un! Yer both absolute characters, I do say. But yes, this is a good chance to get together ‘fore winter sets in for good. Best make it a proper family day. I’ve a mind to bung in the board games later. Not th’ complicated ones, mind you. Don’t think I’d last five minutes at Cluedo wi’ that lot ‘round here!      A proper family day – I’m in. You know, I was just thinkin’ how I’ve not played Cluedo in ages. Not since we had that time when Auntie Pat ended up quoting the entire Bible in the whodunit. It took an hour just to set it up after that.      Oh, go on then! Bring it on! I’m game for anything that makes me feel younger, even if it’s just the box label!      Aye, I’m with you, luv. Although I think I’ll start off quietly by just supervising the loo again. But if ‘tis asked, I’m happy to lend a hand. Or my cunning detective skills. Probably best not to test ‘em though, eh?

I can't get the satnav to work propper, an’ we need t’ get t’ that gig in Newcastle by eight. I jist don’t want t’ lose time by taking a wrong turn agin. Let me have a fiddle wi’ it. Ten out o’ ten een time I find a better route if I scroll down. Dunnae panic now – we’ve got a clean hour before we need t’ be in. Oh aye, an’ who's road journey wasn't plagued by tech firsh when you're in a rush? Still, I'd fetch the old map any day o’ this box talkin' t’ me in a posher accent than mine. You’ve met enough eccentric folk at ceilidhs t’ know posh accents are relative, love. I think it turned round at the last roundabout by the Woolworths. I've driven that route 'fore. Aye, an' you ever looked at that shopping centre as if it's the Tower o' London, expectin' knights t’ pop out round the corner. Remember when we got stuck in that cow grid as if they were humanely sent t’ mock us on the way to the ceilidh last year? How can I forget? I got a sneaky comment from that farmer’s daughter as we were stuck somethin’ to do wi’ the weather an’ the ‘city folk’s hills’ as she put it. Tales t’ tell at the wedding, innit? I can already picture what you’ll serve at it. Or should I say, what you  won't  serve in a nod t’ tradition about nowhere being far from a field? Ha, I'm going for a mix o’ heritage an’ whim. Got some wool crafts comin’ up for the place settings. It’s for the look, no' for use. Although, if someone drops theirs, they might need to fashioned something fresh on the spot. Aye, an’ while the bride is as tight as a drum academically, her granddad’s a poet whos been known to doce o'er at set changes in the ceilidh. I told 'im to go easy on the clydeside antics. I just hope the weather holds between now an’ the big day. A bit o’ rain’s good for the crops, but not so good for the ceilidh hours after the ceremony under tents that sag like a deflated balloon. Let’s be glad this car isn’t the problem; I jist hope the tracks don’t get stalled by the local fauna again.

I can't believe we've got to finish the project brief for that university building by Friday. They've been piling shit on our plate this week. I’m so ready for a weekend away from blueprints and spreadsheets. Tell me about it. It's been one chaotic brief after another. Got a meeting with the client this week where they changed the design direction three times in an hour. Honestly, I’ve been considering listing my flat on AirBnB just to send them a message. Oh, spare me the drama, mate. Remember when we first worked together? You shouted at the site manager because he said lettuce couldn’t be served with meat for lunch. You were still thinking in terms of budgets and specifications, not sandwiches. Yeah, yeah, and you told the client the café design would be "a bubble of modernist calm". Blah, blah, buzzwords. The only breakfast I received from that agreement was a coffee with a smile in it and a split tray of toast. Still working on the communal housing proposal? I mean, I get the vision, but have we considered that some people would rather put up with broken showers than share their space with six other people who still leave gear in the shower? Oh, absolutely. You ever meet someone who works part-time at a bar, still needs their own room to throw a casual Saturday party of ten people and never brings their phone home? No. Me neither. There’s also this someone at the office who keeps putting me off my toast. It's Karen from the admin team—keeps looking at me like I'm some strange being she recently discovered in the plains of Watford. Oh right, Karen? Her coffee consumption per day is probably equal to the number of project deadlines we've missed this quarter. Not to mention the time she helped unblock the printer that was just rebelling for the day. She's your type. I have no idea what my type is any more. I've been eating toast and jam for breakfast since I was a kid, and now I’m expected to navigate a world where people take 'toast' and demand it "with various herbs and meats". The concept is positively foreign. Maybe you need to go back to basics. Start serving your clients breakfast again so they respect you. Coffee in, coffee out, maybe with a box of granola.

I can't believe the traffic in town today. That car almost ran me off the road at the roundabout. It got me so flustered I nearly missed your lane altogether! How do you stay so calm behind the wheel? Honestly, I kind of panic a bit too when it gets busy. I'm still new, remember? But I'm slowly getting the hang of it. Dad helped me with a few practice runs before I got my license. Oh, I'm sure it’s just a matter of time before you're driving like a pro. Just remember to keep your distance and don’t tense up too much. Taking deep breaths works for me when the roads are chaotic. Thanks, I’ll keep that in mind. : Right, so you've got this journalist post at that radio station in Manchester, haven't you? I read the listing the other day. As a language teacher, I’ve read hundreds of applications—media jobs, academic roles, you name it. You know I like dissecting them like a grammar puzzle! So what are the main focuses of the role they’re advertising?     : The keyword is 'audience engagement'. They’re looking for someone who can create content that really resonates with a younger demographic, drive in-depth features, and be part of a production team. They also want experience in working under tight deadlines, handling multiple platforms, and collaborating with technical and editorial staff.     : Got it. So they’re not just looking for a producer, but a storyteller—someone who can work rhythmically with a team and is tech-savvy. Are you planning to include your experience at the local station in York?     : Definitely. I did a series on heritage and identity in Yorkshire that ended up doing well in the podcast charts. But I also want to highlight my adaptability. I did some freelance magazine production earlier in the year, and that involved cross-platform content too—articles, social feeds, even short video features.     : That’s all gold. How are you answering that?     : I say something like, ‘I’m passionate about relatable, real-life stories that bridge divides and spark conversations. Maybe you could specify a recent show or initiative of theirs that you admire, and explain why it resonates with your style. Tailoring it like that could really make you stand out.

Rather annoying this new school situation, isn't it? Every time we try to enrol our little Jamie in a nursery or primary school, they’re full up like a mince pie at Christmas.      Aye, we've had the same in Glasgow! The schools can't stretch to cope with the number of new families, especially with all the Polish families moving in. My goodness, their kids are a bit of a mixed bag but they generally do well once they catch on.      What's a "Polish family"?      Oh, dear. That's a question for your mummy.      That's a very British way of putting it, Elise! I'd say they’re a group of people from Poland who've moved here for work, and I think it's marvellous most of the time. Adds to the character.      Well, here in Cambridge, there’s been a mad rush of people moving, thinking this is some magical area with housing to spare. But no—village with ten houses and thirty applications. Remarkable! I remember in my day, as a publisher, supplying only ten books for a book club in a country village—and getting ten orders in a week. You'd think they were about to face annihilation!      Oh, Bertie, you're quite the romantic when it comes to nostalgia. Still, no one can argue that the housing shortage has led to someone needing to live in a barn with a goat in a rush to find a roof.      A barn? Now that’s a look I’d like to see. Though, I would most certainly flinch at the goats.      What's a barn?      Jamie, really, it's a place where you keep sheep, farmers use it.      And now it's doubling up as a human dwelling in a few cases, I suspect. I tried to get my grandson into a junior school just down the road and they said "nearly bursting".      I told mummy I wanted extra meats in my dinner. Can I have extra meats like a man with a beard go for extra on his face?      Jamie, you see Bertie with the beard, he could use what your Daddy used to call "a bit of a zap" and still manage to stand out.      True to say, though I have to confess I've been grooming at the same spot since 1962. Good for consistency.      That's romanticism, Bertie. Not very British.

A few more miles in the park would do wonders about now. I hear the Lichfield Half Marathon is going to be back on for this year.      Oh that sounds lovely. I haven't run for quite some time, but I've thought about it. To be honest, I've been quite tempted to join a local gym after hearing about some nice classes.      A little bit of exercise is the best medicine, and I reckon being out with the grandkid would do you a world of good! They're such an easy-going thing you've got there. Smart head on her shoulders, I reckon go far in life.      Oh thanks. I made her some popcorn, but I had to be careful with the sugar content.      You are the caring sort!

I can't believe the weekend’s already gone. That was mad with everything we had to do, don't you think? Oh, I know. I was up until like two on Sunday because of that hen do I worked at. Rather annoying this new car of yours, isn't it, Sarah? Handles like it's made of string and... Well, I’ll not go into the cost yet. I haven’t baked your father's pie in years and I do miss the old taste. It was special, a real family recipe—my wedding pie too, in fact.      Now that’s the spirit! Meat go bad? I’ll see about that. If Harry can’t come, I shall eat the leftovers with the cat.

Rather annoying this language stuff, eh Harry? I’ve been doin’ this Spanish book for ‘ow many weeks now and I still can't muddle through more than a basic conversation. It’s bleedin’ impossible for someone me age to pick up the gist of things!      Aye een, I know wot yeh mean, Darlene. I tried that app as well, with the flash cards and all, but me brain’s too old to remember much past “hola” and “gracias.” We’ve both got the same problem—too much gob yet too few results.      That app does  not  work for me. What I found useful was goin’ to that My Spanish Club down by Liverpool Street. Fun atmosphere and we tried to chat, everyday stuff like the weather, goin’ to the shops. Even if we stuffed it up, the teacher would correct us. Felt like actually speakin’ it, which I reckon is important.      Oh, right, I’ve never been for none of them classes. I tried one of them online courses once, y’know the one that’s like lectures and grammar drills and tests and all that deadly stuff. I bloody failed the first test, so I gave it up. They made me hate French in secondary school with all that conjugating.      Aye, I do remember Latin in school—bleedin’ nightmare. So much more exciting than actual languages, eh?      I heard Spain’s got a different way round language learning, especially where Catalan an’ Castilian mix. Kids grow up speakin’ two languages from the get-go. No one worries if they mix them up.      Oh? I did read that too. Like in the north-east where Barcelona is, it’s very different from, say, Madrid. People just speak the two naturally as if they were born with a bilingual switch in their head. I wish I had that switch, Darlene. Me brain just goes,  tiddle tiddle , and points to the go-to bin.      That’s exactly it—no struggle in language-learning regions like Catalonia. People just pick it up through what they hear and say. It’s like fluency by osmosis, innit?      It gives me more of a reason to get over to Madrid one day and practice! Maybe I’ll go there and just sit in a café for a week and get it by osmosis like you said!

Right, I don't suppose we're going to get through all of this paperwork in one go, but let's start with the most important stuff—banking documents and tax stuff. Scanning sounds better than breakfast, honestly. My eyes aren't what they used to be. Speaking of, you ever looked at that flight you booked to see the old man in Spain? It’s kind of like your recipes—just instead of ingredients, we have phrases and context.      Right ho. Let’s not get too technical with this lot. I’ve scanned my will and insurance policies. That's where you start, right?      Exactly. After we get that sorted, maybe we can get you set up with a digital system? It’s not complicated. I could walk you through it.      That would be brilliant, lad. You always were the clever one.

You deserve a break, love. Why don’t we take the bebop and drive up north tomorrah? Get out of the muck for a bit — and I’ll make sure it’s a decent service station, no worries.

Rather skip the new barista café near the station, have you tried it? I mean, they say it’s got the best cold brew in town now.      No, I haven’t, to be honest. I tend to stick to the same old corner coffee shop—it’s cheap and they always know what I want. Though the barista there   does   have the habit of chatting me up a bit too much these days. Not that I’m complaining, mind.      Haha, you and me both, Edith. Funny how people in service industries think they know you after two months of buying a latte. Aye, well I reckon goin’ on about Gantt charts or not, you two have made my line of work sound like child's play in comparison. Time to lay off your elite jobs and come over for dinner. Oh, I’ve not gotten round to  Trapped . I’m into crosswords most evenings. But I quite fancy trying something intense soon, you know, switch off the brain. Just don’t expect me to leave the house before noon. I’ve got this looming appraisal I’ve been dodging like the plague. Honestly, it feels like writing a thesis in two hours.

Rather annoying when the new boots don't fit right, innit? I was out in Chester ‘ere like... got them in some shop an’ now me foot’s killin’ me.      Aww, don’t blame you! I’ve done that before. Went out for a Saturday eenin’ an’ didn’t even think ‘bout proper shoes. First pint an’ I couldn’t even feel me heels no more.      Yer, but heels are a faight ain’t they? Me and Leeds High Street once— Didn’t even get to the bar ’fore I had to sit down with them!      That’s real, only if yer stressed about lookin’ cute, innit?
