Honestly, I'd rather not date anyone at all than go through the shite of pretending I'm someone I'm not for them to like me. We’re allowed to be proud of our roots. Even if it comes with a bit of mud and rain!      Defo. But serious now – are we talking about the trip to go and see my nan up in Cumbria again next weekend? You’re coming in, yeah, Bec?      Aye, if it’s the same trip as the one to see Joe and Nik after, yeah. I need to visit that new mural he’s doing in Keswick. Sounds proper mad.

I can't believe your parents are visiting us for the first time! I've been here in Sussex for a year and haven't been able to meet them yet. Are they staying long? I've fixed up the spare room for them. Not quite as stylish as the rest of the flat, but it'll make do. I'm assuming they liked the cream tea I bought? I tried to explain the scone pronunciation properly, but you should've seen your dad’s face when I said "scones" like it was one syllable! They’re staying for the weekend. Apparently, Grandma wants to try some of my frozen samosas again. I’m still not used to her asking for six at once! Honestly, she’s well into her eighties and still thinks she can eat like a teenager. And I’m terrified my flat will upset them. Mum keeps joking about the little kitchen—something about it being a "closet with breakfast." Maybe I should tidy this up. I feel like I’ve been living out of takeaway containers for weeks. Well, I liked the flat, darling. Clean, practical, and you’ve got proper windows. My Florence never had two decent windows! Still, I didn't expect to find plastic bags everywhere. Make something out of them, dear. Maybe a quilt. You know I used old curtains for ones before. I didn’t mind the samosas, either. Though I reckon the kitchen could do with a spruce up. And I must say, I liked the mention of the care assistant someone mentioned in the village—sounds like a friendly sort of place. Oh, you had the samosas too? Florence, I made sure they were filled with fenugreek and coriander—I about blocked up my lungs eating the first one. And the window cleaning is on me. I’ve already arranged the local chap to do it. I’m not cruel. Still, I must say, this flat gives off the "poor renter" vibe. Nothing wrong with it, mind you. But I was thinking, dear, maybe I could start helping ANON with the utility bills. As a bit of a care professional, I know how things stack up. Well, if we’re going over bills and habits, I’ve been meaning to ask someone—did you go to Brighton on your own again? I mean, you two have been college friends for years.

Rather annoying this wet weather, eh? You’d think in Cambridge we’d know if it’s ‘goin’ to stop or not by now. I’m more used to the blasts of wind we get in Sunderland, but this… this is just soggy and boring as!      Yeah, I saw the forecast earlier and it said “high chance of drizzle” like it wanted to sound fancy. I’ve only been here for a couple of weeks and I’m already sick of seeing rain clouds. Still, it’s nice and quiet in the cafes here when it’s raining, don’t you think?      Oh, I’ll give you that, love the people-watching when people trudge past in the rain, all with umbrellas. Fun to watch the tourists pretending they know where they’re going, don’t they? I mean, the history of Cambridge is grand, but the signs aren’t always that helpful—haha!      True, and the gingerbread here is actually amazing, by the way. I was working on a few details for that new project over the weekend, and I found this shop—Brêtige if you wanna try it.      Oh, sounds nice. I’ve been spending a lot of time online collating data for my current project at work. Corpus compiling isn’t the flashiest job, but it’s the one I’m in for now. Honestly, I’d consider something else if the universities didn’t pay so well for people like me who dabble in data.      That’s oddly enviable. I’m still looking at some property in the area and being an engineer is all about analysing figures, but when it comes to house prices... it’s all sideways. Have you noticed that? I had a look at what my budget could do and it was grim!      Definitely, I know. My brother tried to buy a flat here for ages and he gave up. Said it was a waste of his time. I think it’s partly because of Cambridge’s uni factor. People come here, live here, and end up being priced out by academics trying to find places too.      Yeah, it's a bit of a mess. Plus, with the weather the way it is, I think it’s more of a commitment to building a life than just picking up and moving somewhere. Although the politics bloke on the telly says it’s all about interest rates.

Rather annoying the new bank manager we've got, isn't it? Handles people like she's got better things to do and I've had to wait twenty minutes more than I'd planned today.
